chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad and Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Karim, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The cursing (li'an) does not occur until the man copulates with his wife.

key_terms.اللِّعَانُ: Li'an, the ritual of mutual cursing between spouses to prove or disprove adultery.
key_terms.بِأَهْلِهِ: With his wife, literally 'with his private part', a euphemism for the wife in this context.
key_terms.يَدْخُلَ: He enters/copulates, referring to sexual intercourse (consummation of marriage).

ai.seo_question: When does the ritual of Li'an become valid according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies a key juristic condition for the validity of Li'an, asserting that the ritual is not legally effective until consummation of the marriage has occurred. This ruling is significant in Shia fiqh as it distinguishes between mere betrothal and established marital status, ensuring the curse applies to a true husband-wife relationship. The condition underscores the importance of physical union in validating the specific legal consequences of Li'an, such as the exclusion of paternity claims.
